arxiv-2207-04952.description: Abstract Abstract The coupling between two or more objects can generally be categorized as strong or weak. In cavity quantum electrodynamics for example, when the coupling strength is larger than the loss rate the coupling is termed strong, and otherwise it is dubbed weak.

arxiv-2312-03947.description: Abstract The classical chemostat is an intensely investigated model in ecology and bio/chemical engineering, where n-species, say x 1 , x 2 ​ … ​ x n x_{1},x_{2}...x_{n} compete for a single growth limiting nutrient. Classical theory predicts that depending on model parameters, one species competitively excludes all others.

arxiv-2402-02647.description: Abstract The underwater radiated noise (URN) emanating from ships presents a significant threat to marine mammals, given their heavy reliance on hearing. arxiv-2510-03785.title: On the Duality Between Quantized Time and States in Dynamic Simulation
arxiv-2510-03785.creator: Liya Huang, Georgios Tzounas
arxiv-2510-03785.description: Abstract This letter introduces a formal duality between discrete-time and quantized-state numerical methods. We interpret qss ( qss ) methods as integration schemes applied to a dual form of the system model, where time is seen as a state-dependent variable. This perspective enables the definition of novel qss -based schemes inspired by classical time-integration techniques.

pmc-11696391.title: Synthesis and Reactivity of an Olefin Metathesis-Catalyzing Ruthenium Complex with a Selenoether Moiety in the Benzylidene Ligand
pmc-11696391.creator: Tsubasa Kinugawa, Seishu Mitsusada, Naoki Orito, Takashi Matsuo
pmc-11696391.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A Hoveyda–Grubbs (HG)-type olefin metathesis complex with a selenoether moiety at the terminus of phenoxy moiety was synthesized. The complex showed direct selenium-atom coordination to the ruthenium center, resulting in higher thermodynamic stability compared with the parent HG catalyst. The selenium atom binding enhanced the tolerance to protic solvent molecules in ring-closing metathesis of N-tosyldiallylamide and diethyl diallylmalonate, and also in the cross metathesis between 3-butenylbenzoate and methyl acrylate.
